key_insight: A high-fidelity transonic-wing dataset couples aerodynamic and structural responses to benchmark machine learning for multidisciplinary wing design.
engineering_relevance: The dataset supports ML surrogates that could accelerate wing design while accounting for both aerodynamic performance and structural integrity.
method: Parameterize wing planforms and airfoil sections using geometric variables and class-shape transformation.
Perform static aerostructural analyses across Mach number, angle of attack, altitude, and structural load factor.
Train ML models to predict aerodynamic surface quantities, integrated performance, and wingbox failure distributions.
evidence_signal: The dataset contains 2,471 samples plus 3 out-of-distribution samples; reported ML NRMSE is at most 0.0309 for aerodynamic quantities and 0.1189 for wingbox failure distributions.
watch_item: Only three out-of-distribution samples are included, limiting evidence of generalization beyond the sampled design and operating conditions.
paper_title: High-Fidelity Aerostructural Dataset of Transonic Wings in Cruise Conditions
